1: // Streaming image generation.
2: //
3: // The OpenAI images endpoint streams progressive renders when asked for them:
4: // `stream: true` plus `partial_images: n` turns the response into SSE carrying
5: // `image_generation.partial_image` events (each with a full base64 PNG of the
6: // image so far) followed by `image_generation.completed`.
7: //
8: // Servers that ignore `stream` answer with plain JSON instead, so the reader
9: // below accepts either shape and the caller gets the same result either way.
10: 
11: export interface ImageStreamEvent {
12: 	type: string;
13: 	b64_json?: string;
14: 	partial_image_index?: number;
15: 	error?: { message?: string };
16: }
17: 
18: export const PARTIAL_IMAGE_EVENT = "image_generation.partial_image";
19: export const COMPLETED_IMAGE_EVENT = "image_generation.completed";
20: 
21: /**
22:  * Incremental SSE parser. Feed it chunks in arrival order; it returns the
23:  * events completed by that chunk and buffers the rest. Only `data:` payloads
24:  * are decoded — the `event:` line duplicates the payload's own `type` field.
25:  */
26: export function createSseParser(): (chunk: string) => ImageStreamEvent[] {
27: 	let buffer = "";
28: 	return (chunk: string): ImageStreamEvent[] => {
29: 		buffer += chunk;
30: 		const events: ImageStreamEvent[] = [];
31: 		// Records are separated by a blank line; \r\n is legal in SSE.
32: 		const records = buffer.split(/\r?\n\r?\n/);
33: 		buffer = records.pop() ?? "";
34: 		for (const record of records) {
35: 			for (const line of record.split(/\r?\n/)) {
36: 				if (!line.startsWith("data:")) continue;
37: 				const payload = line.slice(5).trim();
38: 				if (!payload || payload === "[DONE]") continue;
39: 				try {
40: 					const parsed = JSON.parse(payload) as ImageStreamEvent;
41: 					if (parsed && typeof parsed.type === "string") events.push(parsed);
42: 				} catch {
43: 					// A partial JSON payload means the record was split across chunks
44: 					// in a way the blank-line split missed; drop it rather than throw.
45: 				}
46: 			}
47: 		}
48: 		return events;
49: 	};
50: }
51: 
52: export function isEventStream(contentType: string | null | undefined): boolean {
53: 	return (contentType ?? "").toLowerCase().includes("text/event-stream");
54: }
55: 
56: export function pngDataUrl(b64: string): string {
57: 	return `data:image/png;base64,${b64}`;
58: }
59: 
60: export interface ImageStreamResult {
61: 	b64: string;
62: 	/** How many partial renders arrived before the final image. */
63: 	partialCount: number;
64: }
65: 
66: /**
67:  * Read an SSE image stream to completion, invoking `onPartial` for each
68:  * progressive render. Resolves with the final image.
69:  */
70: export async function readImageStream(
71: 	stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>,
72: 	onPartial?: (dataUrl: string, index: number) => void,
73: ): Promise<ImageStreamResult> {
74: 	const reader = stream.getReader();
75: 	const decoder = new TextDecoder();
76: 	const parse = createSseParser();
77: 	let latest = "";
78: 	let final = "";
79: 	let partialCount = 0;
80: 
81: 	try {
82: 		for (;;) {
83: 			const { done, value } = await reader.read();
84: 			if (done) break;
85: 			for (const event of parse(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true }))) {
86: 				if (event.error?.message) throw new Error(event.error.message);
87: 				if (typeof event.b64_json !== "string" || !event.b64_json) continue;
88: 				if (event.type === PARTIAL_IMAGE_EVENT) {
89: 					latest = event.b64_json;
90: 					onPartial?.(pngDataUrl(event.b64_json), event.partial_image_index ?? partialCount);
91: 					partialCount++;
92: 				} else if (event.type === COMPLETED_IMAGE_EVENT) {
93: 					final = event.b64_json;
94: 				}
95: 			}
96: 		}
97: 	} finally {
98: 		reader.releaseLock();
99: 	}
100: 
101: 	// Some servers close after the last partial without a completed event; the
102: 	// most recent partial is the finished image in that case.
103: 	const b64 = final || latest;
104: 	if (!b64) throw new Error("Image stream ended without image data.");
105: 	return { b64, partialCount };
106: }

107: export function lumaHistogram(pixels: ArrayLike<number>, bins = HISTOGRAM_BINS): Float64Array {
108: 	const histogram = new Float64Array(bins);
109: 	const pixelCount = Math.floor(pixels.length / 4);
110: 	if (pixelCount === 0) return histogram;
111: 	for (let i = 0; i < pixelCount; i += 1) {
112: 		const offset = i * 4;
113: 		// Rec. 601 luma; the exact weights matter less than being consistent.
114: 		const luma = 0.299 * pixels[offset] + 0.587 * pixels[offset + 1] + 0.114 * pixels[offset + 2];
115: 		const bin = Math.min(bins - 1, Math.floor((luma / 256) * bins));
116: 		histogram[bin] += 1;

118: 	for (let i = 0; i < bins; i += 1) histogram[i] /= pixelCount;
119: 	return histogram;

1: /**
2:  * Microphone capture on the audio rendering thread.
3:  *
4:  * The deprecated ScriptProcessorNode runs its callback on the main thread, so
5:  * any React render or tool execution during a live session shows up as dropped
6:  * or glitched microphone audio. An AudioWorklet runs on the audio thread and is
7:  * unaffected by main-thread work.
8:  *
9:  * The worklet is shipped as a source string and loaded from a blob URL rather
10:  * than a separate bundled entry point — worklet modules cannot share the app's
11:  * module graph anyway, and this keeps it working under any bundler config.
12:  */
13: 
14: /** Frames per posted chunk. ~85ms at 16kHz: small enough to stay responsive. */
15: const CHUNK_FRAMES = 1365;
16: 
17: const WORKLET_SOURCE = `
18: class PcmCaptureProcessor extends AudioWorkletProcessor {
19:   constructor(options) {
20:     super();
21:     this.chunkFrames = (options && options.processorOptions && options.processorOptions.chunkFrames) || ${CHUNK_FRAMES};
22:     this.buffer = new Float32Array(this.chunkFrames);
23:     this.offset = 0;
24:   }
25: 
26:   process(inputs) {
27:     const channel = inputs[0] && inputs[0][0];
28:     // No input yet (or the track ended): keep the processor alive regardless.
29:     if (!channel) return true;
30: 
31:     for (let i = 0; i < channel.length; i += 1) {
32:       this.buffer[this.offset] = channel[i];
33:       this.offset += 1;
34:       if (this.offset === this.chunkFrames) {
35:         // Convert on the audio thread so the main thread only sees bytes.
36:         const pcm = new Int16Array(this.chunkFrames);
37:         for (let j = 0; j < this.chunkFrames; j += 1) {
38:           const sample = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, this.buffer[j]));
39:           pcm[j] = sample < 0 ? sample * 0x8000 : sample * 0x7fff;
40:         }
41:         this.port.postMessage(pcm.buffer, [pcm.buffer]);
42:         this.offset = 0;
43:       }
44:     }
45:     return true;
46:   }
47: }
48: 
49: registerProcessor("keating-pcm-capture", PcmCaptureProcessor);
50: `;

69: /** Base64-encode raw PCM bytes for transports that carry audio inside JSON. */
70: export function encodePcmChunk(buffer: ArrayBuffer): string {
71: 	const bytes = new Uint8Array(buffer);
72: 	let binary = "";
73: 	// Chunked to avoid blowing the argument limit on long buffers.
74: 	const stride = 0x8000;
75: 	for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += stride) {
76: 		binary += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(i, i + stride));

78: 	return btoa(binary);

83:  * Falls back to a ScriptProcessorNode where AudioWorklet is unavailable.
84:  */

86: 	sampleRate: number;
87: 	onChunk: (base64: string) => void;

92: 	const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true });

95: 
96: 	let disposed = false;
97: 	let teardown = () => {};
98:

102: 			numberOfInputs: 1,
103: 			// AudioWorklet processors are only pulled when they participate in an
104: 			// active output graph. Keep one silent output connected to the
105: 			// destination so microphone frames continue to reach the port without
106: 			// echoing the microphone back to the learner.
107: 			numberOfOutputs: 1,
108: 			processorOptions: { chunkFrames: CHUNK_FRAMES },
109: 		});

111: 		silentOutput.gain.value = 0;

114: 		};
115: 		source.connect(node);
116: 		node.connect(silentOutput);
117: 		silentOutput.connect(context.destination);
118: 		teardown = () => {
119: 			node.port.onmessage = null;
120: 			try { node.disconnect(); } catch {}
121: 			try { silentOutput.disconnect(); } catch {}
122: 		};
123: 	} else {
124: 		const processor = context.createScriptProcessor(4096, 1, 1);
125: 		processor.onaudioprocess = (event) => {
126: 			if (disposed) return;
127: 			const input = event.inputBuffer.getChannelData(0);
128: 			const pcm = new Int16Array(input.length);
129: 			for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i += 1) {
130: 				const sample = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, input[i]));
131: 				pcm[i] = sample < 0 ? sample * 0x8000 : sample * 0x7fff;
132: 			}
133: 			options.onChunk(encodePcmChunk(pcm.buffer));
134: 		};
135: 		source.connect(processor);
136: 		// A ScriptProcessorNode only runs while connected to a destination; the
137: 		// output buffer is left silent so the mic is not echoed back.
138: 		processor.connect(context.destination);
139: 		teardown = () => {
140: 			processor.onaudioprocess = null;
141: 			try { processor.disconnect(); } catch {}
142: 		};
143: 	}
144: 
145: 	return {
146: 		context,
147: 		stream,
148: 		stop() {
149: 			if (disposed) return;
150: 			disposed = true;
151: 			teardown();
152: 			try { source.disconnect(); } catch {}
153: 			try { void context.close(); } catch {}
154: 			stream.getTracks().forEach((track) => track.stop());
155: 		},
156: 	};
157: }

1: // Progressive rendering of in-flight tool arguments.
2: //
3: // While the model writes an `animate` call, the agent emits `toolcall_delta`
4: // events carrying raw JSON argument text. That text is incomplete by
5: // definition — it stops mid-string, sometimes mid-escape-sequence — so it
6: // cannot be JSON.parse'd. These helpers pull a single string field out of the
7: // partial text so the authored HTML can be shown as it arrives.
8: 
9: /**
10:  * Extract the value of a top-level string field from partially-written JSON.
11:  *
12:  * Returns the decoded value so far, or null when the field has not started.
13:  * Handles the truncation cases that matter: a cut mid-escape (`\` or `\uXX`)
14:  * is dropped rather than mis-decoded.
15:  */
16: export function extractPartialJsonString(partialJson: string, field: string): string | null {
17: 	const key = `"${field}"`;
18: 	const keyIndex = partialJson.indexOf(key);
19: 	if (keyIndex === -1) return null;
20: 
21: 	// Advance past the key, its colon, and any whitespace to the opening quote.
22: 	let i = keyIndex + key.length;
23: 	while (i < partialJson.length && /\s/.test(partialJson[i])) i++;
24: 	if (partialJson[i] !== ":") return null;
25: 	i++;
26: 	while (i < partialJson.length && /\s/.test(partialJson[i])) i++;
27: 	if (partialJson[i] !== '"') return null;
28: 	i++;
29: 
30: 	let out = "";
31: 	while (i < partialJson.length) {
32: 		const ch = partialJson[i];
33: 		if (ch === '"') break; // closing quote — the value is complete
34: 		if (ch !== "\\") {
35: 			out += ch;
36: 			i++;
37: 			continue;
38: 		}
39: 		// Escape sequence; if it is truncated, stop and keep what we have.
40: 		const next = partialJson[i + 1];
41: 		if (next === undefined) break;
42: 		if (next === "u") {
43: 			const hex = partialJson.slice(i + 2, i + 6);
44: 			if (hex.length < 4) break;
45: 			out += String.fromCharCode(parseInt(hex, 16));
46: 			i += 6;
47: 			continue;
48: 		}
49: 		const simple: Record<string, string> = {
50: 			n: "\n",
51: 			t: "\t",
52: 			r: "\r",
53: 			b: "\b",
54: 			f: "\f",
55: 			'"': '"',
56: 			"\\": "\\",
57: 			"/": "/",
58: 		};
59: 		out += simple[next] ?? next;
60: 		i += 2;
61: 	}
62: 	return out;
63: }

95: 	return {
96: 		start(contentIndex: number, name: string) {

98: 		},
99: 		/** Returns the HTML to render, or null when there is nothing new to show. */
100: 		delta(contentIndex: number, delta: string, name?: string): string | null {
101: 			const entry = buffers.get(contentIndex) ?? { text: "", name: name ?? "", reported: 0 };
102: 			if (name && !entry.name) entry.name = name;
103: 			entry.text += delta;
104: 			buffers.set(contentIndex, entry);
105: 			if (entry.name !== "animate") return null;

107: 			const html = extractPartialJsonString(entry.text, "body");

109: 			if (html.length - entry.reported < minGrowthChars) return null;
110: 			entry.reported = html.length;
111: 			return html;
112: 		},
113: 		topic(contentIndex: number): string | undefined {
114: 			const entry = buffers.get(contentIndex);
115: 			if (!entry) return undefined;
116: 			return extractPartialJsonString(entry.text, "topic") ?? undefined;
117: 		},
118: 		end(contentIndex: number) {
119: 			buffers.delete(contentIndex);
120: 		},

123: 		},

13: export const DEFAULT_LIVE_HISTORY_CHARS = 6000;

15: function turnText(message: unknown): string {
16: 	const content = (message as { content?: unknown }).content;
17: 	if (typeof content === "string") return content.trim();
18: 	if (Array.isArray(content)) {
19: 		return content
20: 			.filter((part) => part?.type === "text" && typeof part.text === "string")
21: 			.map((part) => (part.text as string).trim())
22: 			.filter(Boolean)
23: 			.join(" ")
24: 			.trim();
25: 	}
26: 	return "";
27: }

29: function turnRole(message: unknown): LiveHistoryTurn["role"] | null {
30: 	const role = (message as { role?: unknown }).role;
31: 	if (role === "assistant") return "assistant";
32: 	// "user-with-attachments" carries the same learner intent as a plain turn;
33: 	// the attachments themselves are dropped along with the other non-text parts.
34: 	if (role === "user" || role === "user-with-attachments") return "user";
35: 	return null;

38: export function buildLiveHistory(
39: 	messages: readonly unknown[],
40: 	options: { maxTurns?: number; maxChars?: number } = {},
41: ): LiveHistoryTurn[] {
42: 	const maxTurns = Math.max(0, options.maxTurns ?? DEFAULT_LIVE_HISTORY_TURNS);
43: 	const maxChars = Math.max(0, options.maxChars ?? DEFAULT_LIVE_HISTORY_CHARS);
44: 	if (maxTurns === 0 || maxChars === 0) return [];
45: 
46: 	const turns: LiveHistoryTurn[] = [];
47: 	// Walk backwards so that when the budget runs out it is the oldest turns
48: 	// that are dropped, not the ones the learner just spoke about.
49: 	for (let i = messages.length - 1; i >= 0 && turns.length < maxTurns; i -= 1) {
50: 		const role = turnRole(messages[i]);
51: 		if (!role) continue;
52: 		const text = turnText(messages[i]);
53: 		if (!text) continue;
54: 		turns.push({ role, text });
55: 	}
56: 	turns.reverse();
57: 
58: 	let total = 0;
59: 	const budgeted: LiveHistoryTurn[] = [];
60: 	for (let i = turns.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
61: 		total += turns[i].text.length;
62: 		if (total > maxChars) break;
63: 		budgeted.push(turns[i]);
64: 	}

Keating's mascot is a CRT monitor with a face. In 2.9 it stops being only a metaphor. Open the new /live page and the tutor is in the room with you: full-duplex voice over OpenAI Realtime or Gemini Live, a camera or screen-share feed it can look at, and a live transcript and tool feed running alongside the lesson.

A surface built for one screen

The live session is its own page, not a modal over the chat. The learner's camera or screen becomes the phosphor behind Keating's bezel; when he has nothing to look at, his face takes the screen back. A boot-style status row shows whether the session is listening or speaking, which vision lane is live, and how many frames have reached the model, all matching the boot sequence and landing hero so a live session never feels like a different product.

The whole surface tears down with navigation. A live session holds the microphone, the camera, and a paid socket — leaving it running in a background tab was never an option, so leaving the page ends it immediately.

Duplex voice, with the same teacher either way

Both realtime providers Keating targets are now driven as full sessions through one startLiveSession contract. OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live each get interruption and barge-in handling: a learner who cuts in no longer keeps hearing the sentence they just stopped. Tool calls run during the conversation under a shared lifecycle — requested, started, completed, or failed — and are emitted on a provider-neutral canonical event stream. The /live transcript, the persistence layer, and any alternate UI all consume that same stream, so what gets recorded does not depend on which provider was behind the socket.

Eyes on the work

A live session can capture from the camera or a shared screen. Keating doesn't pretend the two providers see video the same way: Gemini Live has a dedicated video lane capped at one frame per second, while GPT Realtime accepts still images as conversation items. One capture pipeline feeds both, and each provider supplies its own sink.

Every candidate frame is a cost, so static ones are dropped. A normalized luma histogram is computed for each frame and compared to the last; only a meaningful change is sent. A frozen desk or an idle editor no longer burns tokens, but a page scroll or a hand entering frame still gets through. Frames are skipped while the tab is hidden, too.

A voice that remembers the lesson

A voice session opens a separate model connection. Without a seed, the tutor would reintroduce itself mid-lesson and forget what was just discussed in text. Keating now replays recent plain-text turns into the voice session — tool traffic and generative-UI payloads are dropped, since they mean nothing to a speech model and only waste the smaller audio context window — and adopts the real Keating system prompt as instructions. The voice is the same teacher, not a generic assistant that happens to share the microphone.

Budget, not a transcript dump

Replay walks the conversation backwards and keeps the newest turns within a turn and character budget. When the budget runs out it is the oldest turns that are dropped, so a long session does not silently discard what the learner just said.

The microphone moves off the main thread

The deprecated ScriptProcessorNode ran its callback on the main thread, so a React render or a tool executing during a live session showed up as dropped or glitched microphone audio. Keating now captures microphone audio on the audio rendering thread through an AudioWorklet, shipped as a source string and loaded from a blob URL so it works under any bundler. Browsers without AudioWorklet fall back to the old path rather than failing.

Renders that arrive while they are still being made

Image generation and animation authoring are no longer all-or-nothing. The OpenAI images endpoint streams progressive partial renders as SSE events, and Keating publishes each one to a window event so the in-flight tool card shows the newest frame as it resolves. Animation source arrives the same way: while the model writes an animate call, the authored HTML is pulled alive from the partial JSON argument text — even when it stops mid-escape-sequence — so the animation starts rendering before the tool call finishes.

  • Image progress is keyed by request id, so concurrent generations never overwrite each other.
  • Animation updates are gated on a minimum growth step, so an iframe is not re-rendered on every token.

Release integrity

New unit tests pin the frame-capture histogram and dedup policy, the SSE image-stream parser, the partial-JSON string extractor, the live-history budget, the duplex input-mode resolver, and provider tier parity. 299: /**
300:  * Apply a single search/replace edit to a file in the NodePod VFS.
301:  * The search block must match exactly (including whitespace).
302:  */
303: export async function nodePodApplyEdit(edit: SourceEdit): Promise<EditResult> {
304: 	const pod = await getNodePod();
305: 	if (!pod) {
306: 		return { success: false, file: edit.file, message: "NodePod is not available" };
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	let original: string;
310: 	try {
311: 		original = await pod.fs.readFile(edit.file, "utf8");
312: 	} catch (error) {
313: 		return {
314: 			success: false,
315: 			file: edit.file,
316: 			message: `Cannot read file: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
317: 		};
318: 	}
319: 
320: 	const searchNormalized = edit.search.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
321: 	const contentNormalized = original.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
322: 
323: 	if (!contentNormalized.includes(searchNormalized)) {
324: 		return {
325: 			success: false,
326: 			file: edit.file,
327: 			message:
328: 				`Search block not found in file. Ensure the search text matches exactly, including ` +
329: 				`indentation and newlines. File: ${edit.file}`,
330: 		};
331: 	}
332: 
333: 	const occurrences = contentNormalized.split(searchNormalized).length - 1;
334: 	if (occurrences > 1) {
335: 		return {
336: 			success: false,
337: 			file: edit.file,
338: 			message:
339: 				`Search block appears ${occurrences} times in the file. ` +
340: 				`Edit rejected for safety — include more surrounding context to make the search unique.`,
341: 		};
342: 	}
343: 
344: 	if (!preEditSnapshotByFile.has(edit.file)) {
345: 		try {
346: 			const snap = await nodePodCreateSnapshot(`pre-edit-${Date.now()}`);
347: 			preEditSnapshotByFile.set(edit.file, { id: snap.id, data: snap.data });
348: 		} catch {
349: 			// Validation will report rollback as unavailable if snapshot capture fails.
350: 		}
351: 	}
352: 
353: 	const nextContent = contentNormalized.replace(searchNormalized, edit.replace);
354: 	await pod.fs.writeFile(edit.file, nextContent);
355: 
356: 	const linesRemoved = searchNormalized.split("\n").length;
357: 	const linesAdded = edit.replace.split("\n").length;
358: 
359: 	return {
360: 		success: true,
361: 		file: edit.file,
362: 		message: `Edited ${edit.file}: ${linesRemoved} lines removed, ${linesAdded} lines added. Reason: ${edit.reason || "unspecified"}`,
363: 		diff: {
364: 			linesRemoved,
365: 			linesAdded,
366: 			charDelta: edit.replace.length - searchNormalized.length,
367: 		},
368: 	};
369: }

374: export async function nodePodApplyEdits(edits: SourceEdit[]): Promise<{ results: EditResult[]; rollbackSnapshots: Map<string, string> }> {
375: 	const results: EditResult[] = [];
376: 	const rollbackSnapshots = new Map<string, string>();
377: 
378: 	for (const edit of edits) {
379: 		const pod = await getNodePod();
380: 		if (!pod) {
381: 			results.push({ success: false, file: edit.file, message: "NodePod unavailable" });
382: 			break;
383: 		}

385: 		let currentContent: string;
386: 		try {
387: 			currentContent = await pod.fs.readFile(edit.file, "utf8");
388: 		} catch {
389: 			currentContent = "";

392: 		if (!rollbackSnapshots.has(edit.file)) {
393: 			rollbackSnapshots.set(edit.file, currentContent);

395: 
396: 		const result = await nodePodApplyEdit(edit);
397: 		results.push(result);
398: 
399: 		if (!result.success) {
400: 			break;
401: 		}
402: 	}

404: 	return { results, rollbackSnapshots };
405: }

506: 	const startedAt = performance.now();
507: 
508: 	const session: ShellSession = {
509: 		id,
510: 		command,
511: 		args,
512: 		stdout: "",
513: 		stderr: "",
514: 		exitCode: null,
515: 		running: true,
516: 		startedAt,
517: 		durationMs: null,
518: 		ok: false,
519: 		result: "",
520: 	};
521: 
522: 	try {
523: 		const proc = await pod.spawn(command, args, { cwd: "/workspace" });
524: 		proc.on("output", (text: string) => {
525: 			session.stdout += text;
526: 		});
527: 		proc.on("error", (text: string) => {
528: 			session.stderr += text;
529: 		});
530: 		proc.on("exit", (code: number) => {
531: 			session.exitCode = code;
532: 		});
533: 		await proc.completion;
534: 	} catch (e) {
535: 		session.stderr += `\n[spawn error: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}]`;
536: 		session.exitCode = session.exitCode ?? -1;
537: 	} finally {
538: 		session.running = false;
539: 		session.durationMs = Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt);
540: 		session.ok = session.exitCode === 0;
541: 		session.result = session.stdout || session.stderr;
542: 	}
543: 	return session;
